issue_title: bug: InverseSensitivityAnalyzer ignores the criterion argument
issue_body:
## Summary

`InverseSensitivityAnalyzer.calculate_sensitivities(criterion=...)` accepts a `criterion` argument but never reads it. It always traces `SpotDiagram` and uses `rms_radius`, so callers asking for any other metric silently receive RMS-spot sensitivities. This is inconsistent with `MonteCarloAnalyzer.run`, which validates `criterion` and raises on unsupported values.

## Impact

- Silent wrong-metric results: a caller passing `criterion="mtf"` (or anything else) gets RMS spot sensitivities with no warning.
- Inverse tolerance budgeting then allocates tolerances against the wrong performance metric.
- Inconsistent API: Monte Carlo rejects unsupported criteria; inverse sensitivity silently ignores the argument.

## Reproduction

```python
import inspect
from openlens.tolerancing import InverseSensitivityAnalyzer

src = inspect.getsource(InverseSensitivityAnalyzer.calculate_sensitivities)
body = src.split('"""', 2)[-1]
print("criterion referenced in body:", "criterion" in body)   # False
print("only rms_radius used:", 'res["rms_radius"]' in body)     # True
```

Output:

```
criterion referenced in body: False
only rms_radius used: True
```

## Root cause

`openlens/tolerancing.py:689-704` — the method signature declares `criterion: str = "rms_spot_radius"`, but the body constructs `SpotDiagram` and reads `res_nom["rms_radius"]` unconditionally. Compare `MonteCarloAnalyzer.run` at `:566-593`, which defines `SUPPORTED_CRITERIA` and raises `ValueError` for unsupported values.

## Expected behaviour

Either implement the requested criterion (or the supported subset) or validate it the same way `MonteCarloAnalyzer` does and raise `ValueError` for unsupported metrics. The parameter must not be silently ignored.

## Suggested fix

Add the same `SUPPORTED_CRITERIA` check at the top of `calculate_sensitivities` (reusing the Monte Carlo constant), and dispatch to the matching metric or raise. Document the supported set in the docstring. Add tests for the supported criterion and for an unsupported one raising.
pr_title: fix(tolerancing): honour the inverse-sensitivity criterion argument
pr_body:
## Description

`InverseSensitivityAnalyzer.calculate_sensitivities(criterion=...)`
declared a `criterion` argument and never read it. Every call - including
`optimize_limits()` - traced a `SpotDiagram` and read `rms_radius`
unconditionally:

```
criterion referenced in body: False
only rms_radius used: True
```

A caller passing `criterion="mtf"` (or anything else) silently received
RMS-spot sensitivities, and inverse tolerance budgeting then allocated
tolerances against the wrong performance measure. `MonteCarloAnalyzer`, in
the same module, already rejects an unimplemented criterion with a
`ValueError`.

## What changed

- **`openlens/tolerancing.py`** - `InverseSensitivityAnalyzer` now shares
  `MonteCarloAnalyzer.SUPPORTED_CRITERIA` and validates the argument at the
  top of `calculate_sensitivities()`, before any system state is captured or
  traced. An unsupported name raises `ValueError` naming the supported set.
- The docstring documents the argument, the supported value, and the raise.
- Only `"rms_spot_radius"` is implemented today; the validation is what makes
  the parameter meaningful and keeps the two tolerance tools consistent.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #615

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a regression test that fails before this change and passes after
- [x] `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen OPENLENS_SKIP_SLOW=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`
- [x] `black --line-length=100 openlens/ tests/ --check`
- [x] `ruff check`, `flake8`, `mypy`

New module `tests/test_inverse_sensitivity_criterion.py` - four of its five
tests fail on the unfixed code (the fifth pins that the supported criterion
still measures):

- `test_an_unsupported_criterion_raises`
- `test_an_unsupported_criterion_does_not_trace` - validation happens before
  the first `SpotDiagram`
- `test_the_supported_set_is_the_monte_carlo_set`
- `test_a_rejected_criterion_leaves_the_design_alone`
- `test_the_supported_criterion_is_measured`

Full local suite: `Ran 2712 tests ... OK (skipped=35)`; the tolerance suites
(70 tests) pass.
